content.evidence_note: Actual source-used construction and source-linked argument read through the complete core extraction and subsequent applications. No independent whole-proof reproof or external hard-edge-source audit is claimed. Section 8 explicitly leaves adaptive-core verification as the central verification task.
failure_modes: Ignoring G^T u observations leaves an incorrect information model.
A Gaussian hidden block by itself does not control sigma_min of the whole observed-plus-hidden matrix; the square pivot and low-rank-shift removal are essential.
Conditioning the Gaussian prior on a favorable spectral event can destroy the exact posterior calculation.
Treating appended analysis queries or latent Gaussian blocks as available algorithm data changes the problem.
Wishart smallest-eigenvalue or LRA posterior-overlap arguments do not automatically provide this nonsymmetric two-sided spectral claim.
This is a proof method record, not an independently established theorem or a full Hard Family.
content.goal_pattern: Establish a constant failure floor for estimating sigma_min of a fixed nonsymmetric Gaussian matrix after few adaptive two-sided queries, then use separately justified reductions for other tasks.
content.key_choice: Track both U_j=span(u_1,...,u_j) and V_j=span(v_1,...,v_j), rather than a one-sided Krylov span. Augment the conditioning sigma-field after the estimator has output to expose an invertible square pivot, then remove a rank-at-most-2t Schur shift by a measurable kernel restriction.
content.key_relation: With r_j=dim U_j,s_j=dim V_j, Gobs_j=P_Uj G+P_Uj_perp G P_Vj is F_j-measurable and G=Gobs_j+Q_Uj_perp Z_j Q_Vj_perp^T, where L(Z_j|F_j) is standard Gaussian of size (N−r_j)×(N−s_j), almost surely. Lemma 5.2 constructs ell=N−4t>=N/2, Ftilde_t containing F_t and a coupled Z_ell with L(Z_ell|Ftilde_t)=Gin(ell) and sigma_min(G)<=sigma_min(Z_ell), almost surely.
proof_skeleton: Lemma 5.1, pp.8–9: condition on F_{j−1}. Project new left/right vectors onto the two unrevealed complements, obtaining alpha,beta. Orthogonally align each nonzero vector with the first coordinate. The complete new response reveals the first row for alpha and first column for beta, sharing the corner once. The remaining entries are independent standard Gaussian. Transcript-measurable changes of complement bases preserve this conditional law, including zero or dependent queries.

Lemma 5.2, pp.9–10: set q=2t,k=N−q. Extend U_t+GV_t measurably to a q-dimensional Ubar. Append q row-only queries, revealing M=Q_Ubar^T G. Almost-sure invertibility of G gives rank M=q and injectivity on V_t. Extend V_t to q-dimensional Vbar on which M is bijective, and append q column-only queries. These 2q analysis-only queries reveal blocks A,B,C with invertible A, while the remaining k×k block Z is conditionally standard Gaussian given their complete augmented transcript G_t.

Write S=Z−CA^{-1}B. For unit z, the block vector (−A^{-1}Bz,z) has norm at least one and image (0,Sz); hence sigma_min(G)<=sigma_min(S). The shift F=CA^{-1}B has rank at most q. A G_t-measurable left rotation O places its image in the first q coordinates. Write OZ=(Z1;W), with conditionally independent Gaussian blocks of sizes q×k and ell×k, ell=k−q. Put OF=(F1;0), Y=Z1−F1, and choose a measurable isometry V0(Y):R^ell->ker(Y). Given Ftilde_t=G_t join sigma(Y), W remains independent Gaussian, so Z_ell=WV0(Y) is standard square Gaussian. Since OSV0=(0;Z_ell), sigma_min(S)<=sigma_min(Z_ell). Singular-G null events can be assigned arbitrary constructions.

Lemma 5.3 and Theorem 5.4, pp.12–13: import the hard-edge interface c_he s<=P(sigma_min(Gin(k))<=s/sqrt(k))<=C_he s for k>=1,0<s<=1. Choose b=min(1,1/(4C_he)), a=b/16. The unconditional high event sigma_min(G)>=b/sqrt(N) has probability p_plus=3/4; uniformly ell in [N/2,N], the fresh-core low event at a/sqrt(N) has probability at least p_minus=c_he a/sqrt(2). Conditioning on Ftilde_t transfers this low-event floor to G. For an F_t-measurable estimate use E={estimate>=b/(4sqrt(N))}. Factor-two failure is at least p_minus P(E) and at least p_plus−P(E), giving gamma=p_minus p_plus/(1+p_minus)>0.

Worked downstream application: §6 turns a uniformly successful 3/5 constant-residual solver into a highly reliable inverse-norm estimator through verified fresh-seed amplification, refinement and approximate inverse power. §7 supplies separate residual-to-full-gap bridges and exact two-ordinary-matvec simulations for the two game geometries; these bridges are not implied by the posterior identity alone.
content.required_inputs: G in R^{N×N} has iid N(0,1) entries and is sampled once. The complete algorithm seed is independent of G and included in F0. Query j is an arbitrary measurable function of that seed and previous complete joint responses, returning (Gv_j,G^T u_j). F_j contains the seed and all query-response pairs. Orthonormal frames, complements, images and kernel bases use a fixed measurable selection convention. For fresh-core extraction the actual algorithm has at most t joint queries, t integer in [0,floor(N/8)], with early stopping padded by zero queries. Analysis-only appended queries occur after output and are not revealed to the original algorithm.
transfer_obligations: Re-establish the full conditional law for any changed prior, feedback, precision or seed dependence; observations from both sides must be conditioned on.
Keep the post-output augmentation analysis-only; outputs must remain measurable with respect to the original transcript.
Check measurable frame selection, pivot rank/invertibility, dimensions and residual independence under each enlarged sigma-field.
Use actual target output/loss and prove its information-to-error bridge; a posterior decomposition alone is not game hardness.
Recompute confidence margins and all query units. Theorem 5.4 is a gamma failure floor, not a universal 1/3 lower bound.
For game transfer preserve each geometry's normalization, dimension threshold, fresh rotation and full-gap recovery conditions.
